findings.claim: The current-write validator incorrectly permits continuation_context on resumable receipts that are not sourced from a named campaign, violating the required ownership boundary and allowing named-campaign continuation state into unrelated durable writes.
evidence: skills/slice-supervisor/references/receipt-schema.md:104-107 limits the projection to current named-campaign resumable writes and requires other terminal cases to omit it.
skills/slice-supervisor/SKILL.md:139-145 distinguishes named-campaign continuation projection from non-named terminal receipt handling.

skills/slice-supervisor/scripts/append_metrics.py:610-619 computes named_campaign but uses it only to require missing context for named resumable writes; the omission check applies only when the receipt is nonresumable, so an unnamed resumable receipt carrying continuation_context falls through and is returned as valid at line 620.

skills/slice-supervisor/tests/test_append_metrics.py:477-504 checks missing context for a named resumable write and context on a nonresumable write, but does not exercise the contradictory unnamed-resumable-with-context path.

Contradictory path checked with an in-memory schema-v4 accepted receipt having more_in_scope_work_remains=true, valid continuation_context, and no producer_metrics.campaign_source: validate_current_write returned the record successfully. The failure mechanism is therefore executable, not merely inferred from control flow.

limitations: Review was restricted to the nine listed snapshot artifacts and case packet; no repository history, unrelated files, or internet sources were inspected.
Write-producing test suites were not run because the review was required to remain read-only; the acceptance-critical branch was verified with a bytecode-disabled, in-memory validator invocation.
The supplied artifact hashes matched the case packet.
